title: Take the water back
hook: Push water down any open route until none is left. You can still be one short.

doesNotKnow: that sending flow back along a pipe can increase the total

misconception: Push water along any open route until none is left, and you have the most water possible.
objective: The learner can explain that pushing s-a-b-t first blocks every forward route at a total of 1, that sending that unit back along a-b opens s-b-a-t for a total of 2, and that 2 is the most because only 2 pipes leave s (the smallest cut).

claims.text: With five one-unit pipes s-a, s-b, a-b, a-t, b-t, pushing s -> a -> b -> t first leaves every forward route with a full pipe: stuck at a total of 1.
claims.source: Builder's node check of forward-only greedy pushes: starting with s-a-b-t gives 1; starting with s-a-t or s-b-t gives 2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Own greedy forward-only simulation: zig first 1; s-a-t first 2; s-b-t first 2.

claims.text: Sending that unit back along a-b opens s -> b -> a -> t, for a total of 2.
claims.source: Residual network after the first push has s-b, b-a (reverse of a-b) and a-t free; augmenting along it gives flows s-a 1, s-b 1, a-t 1, b-t 1, a-b 0. CLRS 3rd ed. 26.2. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Residual after zig: s-b, b->a (reverse), a-t free; augment gives all four outer pipes at 1, a-b 0, total 2.

claims.text: Both pipes out of s are full, so nothing can beat 2: no flow is bigger than the smallest cut.
claims.source: Builder's node enumeration of s-t cuts: {s} 2, {s,a} 3, {s,b} 2, {s,a,b} 2; minimum 2. Any flow is at most the capacity of any cut: CLRS 3rd ed. 26.2, Corollary 26.5. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Own cut enumeration: {s} 2, {s,a} 3, {s,b} 2, {s,a,b} 2; min 2. CLRS 3rd ed. Corollary 26.5.

claims.text: Letting a new route cancel an earlier push is how the Ford-Fulkerson method fixes greedy mistakes; when no route is left, the flow equals the smallest cut.
claims.source: Ford and Fulkerson, 'Maximal flow through a network', Canadian Journal of Mathematics 8 (1956); CLRS 3rd ed. 26.2, Theorem 26.6 (max-flow min-cut). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Ford and Fulkerson, Canad. J. Math. 8 (1956) 399-404; CLRS 3rd ed. 26.2, Theorem 26.6 (max-flow min-cut).

recall.question: A flow method pushes water along routes until no route has room. When can it still be improved?
options: Never: no open route means the most water
When a route that sends some water back along a used pipe would carry more
Only if the pipes are made wider
recall.why: Cancelling part of an earlier push can open a new route, as s -> b -> a -> t did. Only when no such route is left is the flow the most possible, equal to the smallest cut.
